arxiv-1802-07140.creator: Michael Felderer Bogdan Marculescu, Francisco Gomes de Oliveira Neto Robert Feldt Richard Torkar
arxiv-1802-07140.description: Abstract This paper presents background, the basic steps and an example for a testability analysis framework for non-functional properties. I Introduction Testability is a quality attribute that evaluates the effectiveness and efficiency of testing: If the testability of a software artifact is high, then finding faults by means of testing is easier.

arxiv-1805-07073.title: Which evolutionary status does the Blue Large-Amplitude Pulsators stay at? 2018 Which evolutionary status does the Blue Large-Amplitude Pulsators stay at? –
arxiv-1805-07073.creator: Tao Wu, Yan Li
arxiv-1805-07073.description: A 2018 arXiv research paper by Tao Wu, Yan Li. Asteroseismology is a very useful tool for exploring the stellar interiors and evolutionary status and for determining stellar fundamental parameters, such as stellar mass, radius, surface gravity, and the stellar mean density. In the present work, we use it to preliminarily analyze the 14 new-type pulsating stars: Blue Large-Amplitude Pulsators (BLAPs) which is observed by OGLE project, to roughly analyze their evolutionary status.

arxiv-2101-01691.title: Multimagnetic Monopoles
arxiv-2101-01691.creator: D. Bazeia, M. A. Liao, M. A. Marques
arxiv-2101-01691.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by D. Bazeia, M. A. Liao, M. A. Marques. In this work we investigate the presence of magnetic monopoles that engender multimagnetic structures, which arise from an appropriate extension of the SU ⁡ ( 2 ) \rm{SU(2)} gauge group. The investigation is based on a modified relativistic theory that contain several gauge and matter fields, leading to a Bogomol’nyi bound and thus to a first order framework, from which stable multimagnetic solutions can be constructed.

arxiv-2210-10115.title: Optical Two-dimensional Coherent Spectroscopy of Cold Atoms Journal: ol
arxiv-2210-10115.creator: Danfu Liang, Lexter Savio Rodriguez, Haitao Zhou, Yifu Zhu, Hebin Li
arxiv-2210-10115.description: Abstract We report an experimental demonstration of optical 2DCS in cold atoms. The experiment integrates a collinear 2DCS setup with a magneto-optical trap (MOT), in which cold rubidium (Rb) atoms are prepared at a temperature of about 200 μ \mu K and a number density of 10 10 10^{10} cm -3 .

arxiv-2404-18019.title: Constrained Hamiltonian dynamics for electrons in magnetic field and additional forces besides the Lorentz force acting on electrons
arxiv-2404-18019.creator: Hiroyasu Koizumi
arxiv-2404-18019.description: Abstract We consider the forces acting on electrons in magnetic field including the constraints and a condition arising from quantum mechanics. The force is calculated as the electron mass, m e m_{e} , multiplied by the total time-derivative of the velocity field evaluated using the quantum mechanical many-electron wave function.

arxiv-2501-15720.title: ESGSenticNet: A Neurosymbolic Knowledge Base for Corporate Sustainability Analysis
arxiv-2501-15720.creator: Keane Ong, Rui Mao, Deeksha Varshney, Frank Xing, Ranjan Satapathy, Johan Sulaeman, Erik Cambria, Gianmarco Mengaldo
arxiv-2501-15720.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Keane Ong, Rui Mao, Deeksha Varshney, Frank Xing, Ranjan Satapathy, Johan Sulaeman, Erik Cambria, Gianmarco Mengaldo. Identifying Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) topics in sustainability reports, or ESG topic analysis, is essential for assessing a company’s ESG performance. While commonly used for this task, existing NLP approaches face three key challenges: irrelevance , the extracted topics are unrelated to ESG, immateriality , the extracted topics lack meaningful value, and limited organisation , the extracted topics have poor alignment with ESG frameworks.

arxiv-2507-11199.description: Abstract Mutation testing has emerged as a powerful technique for evaluating the effectiveness of test suites for Deep Neural Networks (DNNs). arxiv-2602-09475.title: ArtifactLens: Hundreds of Labels Are Enough for Artifact Detection with VLMs
arxiv-2602-09475.creator: James Burgess, Rameen Abdal, Dan Stoddart, Sergey Tulyakov, Serena Yeung-Levy, Kuan-Chieh Jackson Wang
arxiv-2602-09475.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by James Burgess, Rameen Abdal, Dan Stoddart, Sergey Tulyakov, Serena Yeung-Levy, Kuan-Chieh Jackson Wang. Modern image generators produce strikingly realistic images, where only artifacts like distorted hands or warped objects reveal their synthetic origin. Detecting these artifacts is essential: without detection, we cannot benchmark generators or train reward models to improve them. Current detectors fine-tune VLMs on tens of thousands of labeled images, but this is expensive to repeat whenever generators evolve or new artifact types emerge.

pmc-11563918.creator: Ryan D Makin, Ivana Apicella, Roshni Dholkawala, Shinichi Fukuda, Shuichiro Hirahara, Yoshio Hirano, Younghee Kim, Ayami Nagasaka, Yosuke Nagasaka, Siddharth Narendran, Felipe Pereira, Akhil Varshney, Shao-bin Wang, Jayakrishna Ambati, Bradley D Gelfand
pmc-11563918.description: Inflammasome activation is implicated in diseases of aberrant angiogenesis such as age-related macular degeneration (AMD), though its precise role in choroidal neovascularization (CNV), a characteristic pathology of advanced AMD, is ill-defined. pmc-13053408.creator: Martin Beed, Chit Wong, Rob A Dineen, Louise Berry, Peter G Brindley
pmc-13053408.description: Meningitis and encephalitis affect all ages, are prone to misdiagnosis and outcome can be devastating. We provide this common primer for all in the sepsis “chain-of-survival.” Meningitis equals inflammation/infection of the protective membranes that cover the brain; whereas encephalitis affects the brain parenchyma. Meningitis is more common, but they can co-exist as meningoencephalitis.

pmc-13219619.title: Effects of pneumatic tube systems on next-generation viscoelastic coagulation test devices in septic patients and healthy individuals: Results of the randomized controlled VETaPT trial
pmc-13219619.creator: Martin Mirus, Erik Buehrer, Oliver Tiebel, Christian Schnabel, Jan Beyer-Westendorf, Thea Koch, Lars Thielecke, Peter Markus Spieth, Lars Heubner
pmc-13219619.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Rapid coagulation assessment is essential in critical care to enable timely correction of coagulopathy. Viscoelastic testing (VET) supports this goal but may be affected by mechanical stress during transport by pneumatic tube systems (PTS). As PTS are widely used to expedite sample delivery, evaluating the robustness of next-generation VET and platelet function assays under these conditions is crucial for reliable, time-sensitive diagnostics in intensive care.
